_meta.indication: Treatment of thrombocytopenia in adult patients with chronic liver disease who are scheduled to undergo a procedure

pivotal_trials.design: International, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with thrombocytopenia and chronic liver disease scheduled to undergo a procedure with associated bleeding risk
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients who did not require a platelet transfusion or any rescue procedure for bleeding after randomization and up to 7 days following an elective procedure
pivotal_trials.result: Low baseline platelet cohort: 66% responders on DOPTELET 60 mg vs 23% placebo (difference 43%; p<0.0001)

pivotal_trials.design: International, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study; identically designed to ADAPT-1
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with thrombocytopenia and chronic liver disease scheduled to undergo a procedure with associated bleeding risk
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients who did not require a platelet transfusion or any rescue procedure for bleeding after randomization and up to 7 days following an elective procedure (same primary endpoint as ADAPT-1)
pivotal_trials.result: Low baseline platelet cohort: 69% responders on DOPTELET 60 mg vs 35% placebo (difference 34%; p<0.0001). Note: in Table 4 the primary-endpoint p-value <0.0001 is reported in a single row shared across the ADAPT-1 and ADAPT-2 Low Baseline Platelet Count Cohort difference columns.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥3%) are pyrexia (10%), abdominal pain (7%), nausea, headache, fatigue (4%), and peripheral edema (3%). Treatment-emergent thromboembolic events were reported in 0.4% (1/274) of avatrombopag-treated patients vs 1.3% (2/156) of placebo patients.
target_moa: Orally administered second-generation thrombopoietin (TPO) receptor (c-MPL) agonist that promotes megakaryocyte production, maturation, and platelet formation
companion_dx_detail: There are no companion diagnostic or devices proposed with the application

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the drug is not the first in its class and did not raise unexpected significant safety or efficacy issues

description.text: Added new indication for treatment of thrombocytopenia in adult patients with chronic immune thrombocytopenia with insufficient response to a previous treatment

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides a new indication for the treatment of thrombocytopenia in adult patients with chronic immune thrombocytopenia who have had an insufficient response to a previous treatment.

description.text: Expanded indication to include pediatric patients 6 years and older with persistent or chronic immune thrombocytopenia who had insufficient response to previous treatment

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for expansion of the indication to include pediatric patients 6 years and older with persistent or chronic immune thrombocytopenia who have had an insufficient response to a previous treatment.

summary.text: NDA 210238 was submitted under a supporting document 1 letter dated September 21, 2017 and granted priority review; it was filed October 30, 2017 and approved as a standard (regular) full approval based on two identically designed Phase 3 placebo-controlled trials, without accelerated approval, without referral to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: The sponsor submitted a marketing application for avatrombopag under NDA 210238 supporting document 1 letter dated September 21, 2017.
The sponsor requested priority review which was granted by the agency. The application was filed on October 30, 2017.

Your application for avatrombopag was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this drug is not the first in its class and the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a drug of this class.

requirement.text: PMR 3405-1: Conduct a study in juvenile rats with avatrombopag administration starting on Day 7 post-partum, dosing for 10 weeks with a minimum 4-week recovery period to assess reversibility of adverse effects or developmental delays

citations.quote: PMR 3405-1 Conduct a study in juvenile rats with avatrombopag administration starting on Day 7 post-partum. Dosing duration should be 10 weeks to cover the entire pediatric age range from neonate through adolescence to adulthood. A minimum 4-week recovery period will be included upon completion of dosing to assess reversibility of any adverse effects or delays in development.

citations.quote: PMR 3405-2 Conduct a study to evaluate the bioavailability of an avatrombopag age appropriate formulation relative to the 20 mg tablet formulation in the fed condition, and to evaluate the effect of food on the bioavailability of the age appropriate formulation in healthy adults.
